title: Friendship That Honors God
subtitle: Proverbs describes friendship by behaviour, which you can check.
objectives: Name the scriptural tests of friendship

cards.title: Proverbs describes friendship by behaviour
cards.text: Not by feeling. Which is useful, because behaviour is something you can actually check — in them, and in yourself.

cards.title: Four tests you can run
cards.text: Each one comes from a specific verse.
points: **Will they tell you the truth?** Proverbs 27:6.
**Are they there when it is bad?** Proverbs 17:17.
**Who are you becoming?** Proverbs 13:20.
**Does it cost them anything?** 1 Samuel 18.

cards.title: Six buttons
cards.text: Tap each test. The last one is the hard one.

question.explain: A friend who never disagrees is not doing the job.

cards.title: The one with no exceptions
cards.text: This is the bluntest verse in the set.
points: **"Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise."**
**The second half is the warning.**
**You end up like the people you spend hours with.**
**Not sometimes. This is how people work.**

options: becoming like the people you spend time with

cards.title: What Jonathan actually gave up
cards.text: This is the detail that makes the story more than sentiment.
points: **Jonathan was the king's son.** The throne was his.
**He gave David his robe and his weapons.**
**Those were the symbols of that claim.**
**He gave away his own succession**, on purpose.

cards.title: A good training partner is not easy on you
cards.text: The one who lets you win teaches you nothing.
points: **A partner who goes soft** hides your gaps.
**You find them in a real fight instead.**
**"Faithful are the wounds of a friend"** is literal here.
**You want the one who tells you** your guard drops.

cards.title: You rise or sink to the lobby
cards.text: Anyone who plays competitively has watched this happen.
points: **Play with better players** and you improve.
**Play with people who tilt** and you tilt.
**Nobody decides to copy them.** It happens anyway.
**Proverbs 13:20, in a queue.**

cards.title: The hard test is the last one
cards.text: Every test above, read the other way round.
points: **Do you tell your friends the truth?**
**Are you there in their bad week?**
**Does being your friend cost you anything?**
**That list is harder** than judging theirs.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Proverbs 27:6 — faithful are the wounds of a friend.
Proverbs 17:17 — a friend loves at all times.
Proverbs 13:20 — you become like the people you walk with.
Jonathan gave David his robe and weapons: his own claim to the throne.

quiz.explain: A friend who disagrees with you is doing the job.

quiz.text: What does that verse imply about a friend who always agrees?
options: They are not doing the job

quiz.explain: The bad week is the test.
quiz.objective: Name the scriptural tests of friendship

quiz.text: Proverbs 13:20 says whoever walks with the wise…
quiz.explain: And the second half is the warning.

quiz.text: Proverbs 13:20 allows for exceptions if your intentions are good.
quiz.explain: Hours matter more than intentions. This is how people work.

quiz.explain: The symbols of his own claim.

options: It gave away his own succession

quiz.explain: You find the gaps in a real fight instead.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 8 Devotion. Proverbs describes friendship in terms of behaviour rather than feeling, which makes it testable, and the week is built as four tests with their verses. Proverbs 27:6 is the one most worth having at this age: a friend who never disagrees is not being a friend, which arrives for him naturally through the training-partner lens where the point is literal. Proverbs 13:20 is given without softening, because it is a claim about how people actually work rather than an aspiration. The Jonathan detail — his robe and weapons were the symbols of a throne that was his — is what lifts the story above sentiment.
discussion: Ask what Proverbs 27:6 says and what it implies.
Ask who he spends the most hours with, and what that is making him.
Ask what Jonathan gave up and why it mattered.
Ask him to run all four tests on himself.
extension: Have him apply the four tests to himself in writing, privately.
Have him find 1 Samuel 18:4 and work out what the items represented.
misconceptions: "A good friend always agrees with you." Proverbs 27:6 says the opposite.
"Who I spend time with does not change me." Proverbs 13:20 denies that.
"Jonathan just gave David some clothes." They were the symbols of his claim.
